title: F3 proponent: Stehle anomaly as Caesar shift=5 + width=4 columnar
hypothesis_summary: Anomaly E0a (Stehle 2000, measured by Bean 2021): the 9-character segment DIAWINFBN at carved positions 55-63 has the property that each pair of letters 4 positions apart differs by exactly 5 (mod 26). This is locally interesting but Bean wrote 'harder to measure, explain or exploit'. The proponent reading interprets this as a structural hint at a key offset of 5 operating at interval 4 — i.e. a Caesar shift=5 layer composed with a width-4 columnar route, against the disclosed-crib keyword pool.

provenance_items.quote_or_summary: Anomaly E0a: DIAWINFBN constant-difference property; pairs 4 apart differ by 5 (mod 26). Bean 2021 §2.3, citing Stehle 2000.

composition_templates.rationale: Pure Caesar shift=5 — Stehle anomaly as standalone shift.
LESSON-019 numeric-Caesar + route + columnar: Stehle shift composed with width=4 route and crib-keyword columnar.

constraints: Shift pool restricted to {5}; width pool restricted to {4}; keywords restricted to BERLIN/CLOCK.
caveats: PROPONENT framing for a published statistical anomaly; Bean himself flagged it as hard to exploit.
Stehle property is local to a 9-letter window; extrapolating to a global Caesar shift is structurally aggressive.
